Section 16: Fire safety information.
This regulation applies where building work consists of or includes the erection or extension of a relevant building or a relevant change of use of a building.
The person carrying out the work must give fire safety information to the responsible person no later than the stated completion or occupation deadline.

Appendix A: Key terms.
Access room: A room that the only escape route from an inner room passes through.
Alternative exit: One of two or more exits, each of which is separate from the other.
Alternative escape route: Escape route sufficiently separated from another escape route.
Basement storey: A storey with a floor which at some point is more than 1200mm below the highest level of ground adjacent to the outside walls.
Cavity barrier: Construction provided to close a concealed space against penetration of smoke or flame, or provided to restrict movement of smoke or flame within such a space.
Circulation space: A space mainly used as a means of access between a room and an exit from the building or compartment.
Common parts: Those parts of a building used by occupants of more than one dwelling.
Compartment: A building or part of a building comprising one or more rooms, spaces or storeys constructed to prevent fire spread to or from another part of the same building or adjoining building.
Compartment floor: A fire-resisting floor used to separate one fire compartment from another.
Compartment wall: A fire-resisting wall used to separate one fire compartment from another.
Dead end: Area from which escape is possible in one direction only.
Dwelling: A unit of residential accommodation occupied by a single household.
Dwellinghouse: A dwelling that is not a flat.
Escape route: Route forming part of the means of escape from any point in a building to a final exit.
Evacuation lift: Lift used as part of management arrangements for evacuating people.
Final exit: Termination of an escape route from a building giving direct access to a street, passageway, walkway or open space.
Fire damper: Mechanical or intumescent device within a duct or ventilation opening that is operated automatically and intended to prevent fire passage.
Fire door: Door or shutter provided for the passage of people, air or objects which, together with its frame and furniture, is intended to resist fire passage.
Fire doorset: Complete fire door assembly including door leaf, frame, seals and essential hardware.
Firefighting lift: Lift designed to have additional protection, controls and signals to enable use under direct control of the fire and rescue service.
Firefighting shaft: Protected enclosure containing a firefighting stair, firefighting lobbies and, where provided, a firefighting lift.
Firefighting stair: Protected stairway communicating with accommodation area only through a firefighting lobby.
Fire main: Water supply pipe installed in a building for firefighting purposes.
Fire resistance: Ability of a component or construction to satisfy criteria of loadbearing capacity, integrity and insulation for a stated period.
Fire-separating element: Compartment wall, compartment floor, cavity barrier or construction that separates one fire compartment from another.
Fire-stopping: Sealing or closing an imperfection of fit or design tolerance between fire-separating elements to restrict fire and smoke passage.
Flat: Separate and self-contained premises constructed or adapted for residential purposes and forming part of a building from some other part of which it is divided horizontally.
Gallery: Floor or platform raised above the main floor of a room or space.
Habitable room: Room used, or intended to be used, for dwelling purposes.
Inner room: Room from which escape is possible only by passing through another room.
Maisonette: Self-contained dwelling with accommodation on more than one storey.
Notional boundary: Boundary assumed between buildings on the same site for purposes of space separation.
Place of special fire hazard: Area containing a higher fire risk because of use, contents or process.
Protected corridor: Corridor enclosed with fire resisting construction.
Protected entrance hall: Entrance hall separated from all other rooms in the flat by fire resisting construction and fire doorsets.
Protected lobby: Lobby enclosed with fire resisting construction.
Protected shaft: Shaft that enables services, lifts or stairs to pass from one compartment to another and is enclosed with fire resisting construction.
Protected stairway: Stairway discharged through a final exit to a place of safety and enclosed with fire resisting construction.
Relevant boundary: Boundary used for determining space separation.
Storey exit: Final exit or doorway giving direct access into a protected stairway, firefighting lobby or external escape route.
Unprotected area: Area of external wall that does not have the required fire resistance.
Vehicle access route: Route suitable for use by fire and rescue service vehicles.
